newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Centam leaders say goodbye to Nicaragua's Chamorro.
newsitem.headline: Centam leaders say goodbye to Nicaragua's Chamorro.

text.p: Central America's heads of state arrived in Nicaragua on Monday to bid farewell to President Violeta Chamorro, whose nearly seven-year term in office ends on Jan. 10.

The visiting leaders lavished praise on Chamorro, Latin America's only serving female leader, saying she will be remembered for having brought peace and democracy to a country wracked by decades of brutal dictatorship and civil war.

Violeta Chamorro "is a woman who has made history ... and has won a place in it with her search for peace and reconciliation of the Nicaraguan people," Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares told reporters on arrival. He was joined by leaders from Costa Rica, El Salvador, Honduras, Guatemala and Belize.

Nicaraguan police fanned out in force across Managua to guarantee the presidents' safety, banning the carrying of firearms or explosives and the sale of alcohol near where the presidents were meeting.

The heads of state supported the results of Nicaragua's controversial Oct. 20 elections, crediting them with having strengthened the region's democratic institutions and political stability. The vote was won by Arnoldo Aleman of the right-wing Liberal Alliance but second-place finisher Daniel Ortega of the left-wing Sandinista Front charged fraud.
Honduran President Carlos Roberto Reina congratulated Chamorro for having "permitted a democratic transition that serves as an example for the people of Central America."
The presidents also lauded Guatemala for its announcement that it will sign a treaty ending its three-decade-long civil war, the last civil war in Central America.

Chamorro, 68, the widow of a slain newspaper publisher, came to power in 1990 when she toppled President Daniel Ortega at the ballot box, ending 11 years of Sandinista rule. She also ended the civil war between the Sandinistas and U.S.-backed Contra rebels.
The presidents are slated to discuss regional issues, meet President-elect Aleman and head home on Tuesday.
